items.title: Amos White Interview, 1958-08-23
items.q: I still consider her one of my greatest friends. But she is so, she's such a devout Catholic and a good Christian person. That's right. And it would be shameless for me to say anything different about her. She befriended me so many times.

ctx.x: That's right. He never got to tell me anything about it. That's right.

So, you can tell me a little bit about it. Well, Buck, Buck served the season on the, on the Georgia Smart Set, uh, under Frank Moreland. Uh, and Buck was a featured man in the way he played. And Buck was a very fine jazz man. And he had a distinct way of, of playing the special numbers that Frank would allocate him to play at the Noonday concert was, was a, a send off to the band. The same as after, after I had spent a season in New Orleans down there, and I come to this later, because this is 1924 when I took a…
She rode the horse too, or no?

items.title: Lizzie Miles Interview, 1951-01-18
items.q: That's why Amos came by. He used to come and get me to take me to get fresh air.

ctx.x: Who was in the band? Who else?

Well, now I see, there was Manuel Mineta and there was, um, I can't, I can't, I think, I think Carrie Fritz was the, I think Carrie was the cornet player. And, um, they had a cornet, I think banjo or guitar, I'm not sure, I can't remember so well. But, um, I think there was a piano, either banjo or a guitar, cornet, Amos White was playing the cornet. He's now in Oakland, California, Amos White, cornet player. He was cornet and they had drums and trombone and manual on the piano.
